title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Reverse DCF & Peer Reality

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; implied expectations are what you underwrite. When a company levers up to buy growth, the market demands proof that incremental ROIC exceeds the cost of debt.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

summary: At ₹1,104.90 (₹12,282 Cr market cap on Screener; ₹11,543 Cr on TradingView), Cyient trades at 29.8x–32.5x depressed TTM earnings (₹33.48 EPS) and 2.26x book value. A Reverse DCF on ~₹14,454 Cr Enterprise Value implies ~11.5% 10-year FCF CAGR at an 11.5% WACC—pricing in successful DET margin recovery and TAO Digital / Kinetic integration, while offering limited margin of safety if debt service or working capital drags persist.

web_blocks.html: Our price-blind audit in Chapters 1 through 6 assigned Cyient a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality verdict and PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health [1]. We now examine the market tape as of the 13 November 2026 NSE close [20]. At ₹1,104.90 per share, Cyient carries a Screener market cap of ₹12,282 Cr (TradingView shows ₹11,542.89 Cr post-buyback) [1][20]. The stock sits 13.48% below its 52-week high of ₹1,277.00 and 47.26% above its ₹750.30 low [20].

On trailing multiples, the stock looks optically rich. Screener prints a Stock P/E of 29.8x and TradingView prints 32.47x against depressed TTM EPS of ₹33.48 (TTM PAT ₹404 Cr) [1][20]. It also trades at 2.26x book value (₹459/share) with a 1.45% dividend yield [1][20]. Yet headline P/E misleads in both directions. TTM earnings reflect FY26 restructuring, 33–36% tax rates, and quarterly interest rising from ₹14 Cr to ₹37 Cr [1]. Meanwhile, borrowings surged to ₹2,759 Cr in September 2026 [1]. Adding ₹2,759 Cr gross debt to ₹12,282 Cr equity and subtracting ₹587 Cr investments yields an Enterprise Value (EV) near ₹14,454 Cr [1]. That places Cyient at ~14.0x TTM EBITDA (₹1,029 Cr) and ~20.9x FY26 FCF (₹693 Cr) [1].

web_blocks.html: To test whether ₹1,104.90 offers an edge relative to alternatives, we compare Cyient head-to-head against five NSE-listed Indian ER&D and electronics manufacturing peers using the same-session 13 November 2026 TradingView snapshot [20][21][22][23][24][25].

web_blocks.caption: CYIENT vs. Indian ER&D & EMS Peer Matrix (Verified 13 November 2026 Snapshot)
web_blocks.takeaway: On TradingView TTM multiples, Cyient (32.47x P/E) trades at a discount to Tata Elxsi (35.65x), Tata Technologies (48.23x), and Syrma SGS (68.77x), and at a modest premium to LTTS (29.29x) and KPIT (28.31x), while carrying the highest leverage (0.54x D/E) and lowest ROE (6.98% TV / 8.61% Screener).

web_blocks.mechanism: When an Indian ER&D vendor shifts from pure organic engineering staffing into larger multi-year digital/embedded programs and bolt-on acquisitions, its valuation multiple expands only after EBIT margins stabilize above 15–16% and ROCE holds above 20%. During periods when LTTS's margins compressed or growth slowed to single digits, the stock derated to 25–30x P/E until operating leverage returned.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: LTTS trades at 29.29x TTM P/E on ₹45,034.05 Cr market cap with 20.4% ROE and 0.08x D/E, whereas Cyient's 12.3% ROCE, 6.98% TV ROE, and 0.54x D/E leave less valuation cushion if earnings recovery stalls.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Cyient's multiple will not sustainably expand past 30–32x until consolidated ROCE climbs back above 16–18% and net debt trends down.

web_blocks.html: Our valuation judgment is clear: Cyient is fairly priced at ₹1,104.90, not a deep-value bargain. Its 29.8x–32.5x trailing P/E reflects trough TTM earnings. On normalized FY28E EPS of ₹49–51, the stock trades at ~21.7x–22.5x forward earnings. That is reasonable for a diversified aero, rail, semi, and AI platform. Still, ₹2,759 Cr of debt and 8.61% ROE limit near-term multiple expansion until deleveraging shows up in cash flow [1].
Valuation Trigger: Re-rate target multiples above 27x only if Q3/Q4 FY27 borrowings fall below ₹2,400 Cr and ROCE recovers toward 15%+.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have finished our price-blind audit of Cyient—and walked away with a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality verdict—we finally get to open the market screen and ask the most important question in investing: what is the market already pricing in at today's share price?

As of the verified Friday, 13 November 2026 close on the National Stock Exchange, Cyient trades at ₹1,104.90 per share. That gives the company a market capitalization of ₹12,282 crore on Screener (and ₹11,543 crore on TradingView, reflecting the post-buyback share count adjustment). The stock sits 13.5% below its 52-week high of ₹1,277.00 and 47.3% above its 52-week low of ₹750.30. On the surface, the headline valuation looks steep: Screener prints a trailing P/E of 29.8x and TradingView prints 32.47x against depressed trailing-twelve-month earnings per share of ₹33.48, alongside a 2.26x price-to-book ratio and a 1.45% dividend yield.

Why does a business with 8.61% ROE and 12.3% ROCE command nearly 30x trailing earnings? Because the market is looking past the trough. Remember what we saw in Chapters 5 and 6: TTM net profit of ₹404 crore was weighed down by FY26 restructuring, a spike in effective tax rates to 33–36%, and quarterly interest expense jumping from ₹14 crore to ₹37 crore as Cyient took on debt to buy Kinetic Technologies and TAO Digital. When you strip out the noise and look at Enterprise Value—roughly ₹12,282 crore of equity plus ₹2,759 crore of September 2026 borrowings less ~₹587 crore of investments—you arrive at an Enterprise Value of approximately ₹14,454 crore. Against FY26 Free Cash Flow of ₹693 crore, that is an EV/FCF multiple of roughly 20.9x, and roughly 14.0x TTM operating profit of ₹1,029 crore.

Let us run a Reverse Discounted Cash Flow on that ₹14,454 crore Enterprise Value. Assuming an 11.5% weighted average cost of capital and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, today's price of ₹1,104.90 implies that Cyient must compound its Free Cash Flow at roughly 11.5% per year over the next decade. Think about what that requires in practice. It does not require a miracle, because FY26 FCF of ₹693 crore did not yet include a full year of TAO Digital or Kinetic Technologies, nor did it reflect DET's Q2 FY27 margin rebound to 14.2%. If Sukamal Banerjee holds DET margins above 14%, Cyient Semiconductors scales its custom silicon backlog, and TAO Digital delivers its promised AI and data engineering growth without customer churn, normalized FY28E EPS can plausibly recover to ₹49–51 per share. At a 25.5x multiple, that yields a Base Case fair value of ₹1,280 per share—roughly 15.8% above today's close.

But notice the flip side of that math. Because Cyient is now carrying ₹2,759 crore of borrowings, any stumble in integration, any prolongation of the 119-day cash conversion cycle at Cyient DLM, or any slowdown in aerospace and communications R&D budgets hits equity holders twice—once through lower operating profit and once through higher interest expense. In a Bear Case where FCF growth stalls at 6.5% annually and the market compresses the terminal multiple to 13x FCF, the implied equity value drops to ₹820 per share, representing roughly 26% downside from here. Conversely, in a Bull Case where Cyient Semiconductors becomes a $100M+ high-margin ASIC platform and DET pushes margins back toward 15–16%, FCF compounding of 16.5% could justify ₹1,550 per share.

How does Cyient stack up against its listed Indian peers on the exact same 13 November 2026 TradingView tape? L&T Technology Services (LTTS) trades at ₹4,247.20, a ₹45,034.05 crore market cap, and 29.29x TTM P/E with 20.4% ROE. KPIT Technologies trades at ₹552.00, a ₹15,114.92 crore market cap, and 28.31x TTM P/E. Tata Technologies trades at ₹668.80 (₹27,156.75 crore market cap) and 48.23x TTM P/E, while pure-play electronics manufacturer Syrma SGS trades at ₹1,504.10 (₹29,044.13 crore market cap) and 68.77x TTM P/E. Tata Elxsi trades at ₹3,835.00 (₹23,830.96 crore market cap) and 35.65x TTM P/E. Relative to this cohort, Cyient's 32.47x TTM P/E sits slightly above LTTS and KPIT, yet it carries the highest balance-sheet leverage (0.54x debt-to-equity) and the lowest trailing ROE (6.98% TradingView / 8.61% Screener) in the group.

Here is our independent takeaway from Chapter 7: at ₹1,104.90, Cyient is fairly priced for a turnaround-in-progress, not mispriced as a deep-value bargain. The market has already given Sukamal Banerjee partial credit for Q2 FY27's 25% top-line surge and 14.2% DET margin. To justify committing fresh capital with an asymmetric edge, we need either a pullback toward structural support—where the risk-to-reward math skews decisively in our favor—or hard evidence over the next two quarters that net debt is falling and ROCE is climbing back above 15%.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — Why Enterprise Value Matters More Than P/E Here
book_callouts.text: When a company swaps ₹2,300+ crore of net cash/low-debt balance sheet flexibility for acquisitions and a buyback in a single six-month window, trailing P/E stops telling the whole story. Always anchor on Enterprise Value to Free Cash Flow and track whether incremental operating profit comfortably covers the new interest bill.

book_subsections.title: Deconstructing the Reverse DCF: What ₹1,104.90 Demands From FY27–FY36
paragraphs: When you and I sit across the desk to evaluate a stock trading at ₹1,104.90, the worst mistake we can make is to stare at a single trailing P/E ratio and declare it cheap or expensive. Cyient's 29.8x Screener P/E and 32.47x TradingView P/E are backward-looking snapshots of a transitional year. To see what the market is truly underwriting, we have to flip the model around and ask what cash-flow trajectory justifies a ₹14,454 crore Enterprise Value.

Start with the building blocks. Cyient generated ₹787 crore of Cash from Operations and ₹693 crore of Free Cash Flow in FY26. That ₹693 crore FCF figure did not yet include a full year of earnings from Kinetic Technologies or TAO Digital Solutions, both of which closed during H1 FY27. Nor did it reflect the 14.2% DET EBIT margin achieved in Q2 FY27, which was 180 to 200 basis points higher than the trough quarters of FY26. At the same time, however, the new ₹2,759 crore debt load means Cyient now faces roughly ₹140 to ₹150 crore of annual interest expense—up sharply from ₹61 crore in FY26—plus higher depreciation and amortization from roughly ₹2,937 crore of incremental fixed and intangible assets added to the balance sheet.

If we apply an 11.5% weighted average cost of capital—appropriate for an Indian mid-cap engineering and electronics group carrying 0.54x debt-to-equity—and a 4.5% terminal growth rate, a ₹14,454 crore Enterprise Value requires Cyient's Free Cash Flow to compound at roughly 11.5% per year over the next decade. That means annual FCF must climb from ₹693 crore in FY26 toward ₹1,000 crore by FY29–FY30 and roughly ₹2,050 crore by Year 10. In our Base Case deleveraging bridge, consolidated CFO rises from ₹787 crore in FY26 to ₹920 crore in FY27E and ₹1,120 crore in FY28E as TAO Digital and Kinetic contribute full years; after ₹135–145 crore of capex, ₹115–148 crore of cash interest, and ₹200–240 crore of moderated dividends, Cyient retires roughly ₹1,050 crore of debt over two years, stepping borrowings down from ₹2,759 crore toward ₹1,750 crore. Conversely, if Cyient DLM's 303 inventory days and 119-day Cash Conversion Cycle tie up incremental cash, or if TAO Digital suffers client attrition post-acquisition, free cash flow will stall in the ₹700–₹850 crore range and the stock will re-rate downward toward ₹820.

book_subsections.title: Peer-by-Peer Reality Check: Why Cyient Trails Pure-Play Compounders on ROE
paragraphs: Comparing Cyient against its five NSE-listed peers makes the market's valuation hierarchy crystal clear. L&T Technology Services (LTTS) is the closest multi-vertical ER&D benchmark: at ₹4,247.20 and a ₹45,034.05 crore market cap, LTTS trades at 29.29x TTM P/E—below Cyient's 32.47x TradingView P/E—while delivering 20.4% ROE with just 0.08x debt-to-equity. Tata Elxsi trades at ₹3,835.00 (₹23,830.96 crore market cap) and 35.65x TTM P/E with 23.87% ROE. KPIT Technologies, the pure-play automotive software specialist, trades at ₹552.00 (₹15,114.92 crore market cap) and 28.31x TTM P/E.

Meanwhile, Tata Technologies trades at ₹668.80 (₹27,156.75 crore market cap) and 48.23x TTM P/E, while pure-play electronics manufacturer Syrma SGS trades at ₹1,504.10 (₹29,044.13 crore market cap) and 68.77x TTM P/E. Cyient sits right in the middle of this pack on P/E, yet its 6.98% TradingView ROE (8.61% Screener) and 0.54x debt-to-equity are the weakest balance-sheet metrics in the group. That explains why the market is demanding proof of deleveraging before awarding Cyient a 35x+ multiple.

Think about the LTTS parallel we just examined in the web edition. Between 2019 and 2024, L&T Technology Services proved that an Indian ER&D vendor only earns and holds a 35x+ compounder multiple when EBIT margins stay reliably above 15–16% and ROCE exceeds 20%. Whenever LTTS hit an acquisition digestion phase or an industrial capex pause, its multiple compressed back toward 25–30x until operating leverage returned. Cyient is in that exact proving window right now: its Q2 FY27 DET EBIT margin of 14.2% is a genuine 10-quarter high, but consolidated ROCE of 12.3% still sits nearly 800 basis points below LTTS's historical standard. Until consolidated ROCE climbs back above 16% and net debt trends down, expecting multiple expansion beyond 25–27x normalized FY28E earnings would be wishful thinking.

Let us also check the dividend and buyback signal. Screener shows a 1.45% dividend yield on a 42–49% historical payout ratio, and management retired 64 lakh shares at ₹1,125 in the July 2026 tender-offer buyback. Notice how close that ₹1,125 buyback price is to Friday's ₹1,104.90 close: investors who stayed through the tender offer are sitting right around the price management itself chose to retire equity. That provides a psychological anchor near ₹1,100, but it does not replace the need for fundamental deleveraging over the next four quarters.

One more subtlety in the valuation math deserves your attention: the divergence between Screener's ₹12,282 crore market cap and TradingView's ₹11,543 crore market cap. That ₹739 crore gap stems from how each data feed reflects the post-buyback share count reduction following the July 2026 tender offer (when Equity Capital stepped down from ₹56 crore to ₹52 crore). Regardless of which share-count feed you use, Enterprise Value sits in the ₹13,700 crore to ₹14,454 crore band once you add ₹2,759 crore of September 2026 borrowings and subtract ₹587 crore of investments. On either basis, the market is asking for roughly 11% to 12% annual Free Cash Flow compounding over the next decade—meaning valuation is neither a free lunch nor an obvious bubble, and your entry price relative to structural support is what decides the trade.
